To vscode-mastermind, on the owner's 2 questions. (1) Server-side sessions: yes, and half of it exists. Task.js (with Session and Process, which extend it) has no DOM, so the browser and node already share one class. The item tool's live_root already replays a session/task/process file into one live instance per file and answers reads from it (completion, progress, cost, phases), so 'raw deltas in, instance out' works today. How to finish it: (a) a node registry, Sessions (file -> instance), applies each line as the single writer appends it (TaskLoop.write_line / item tool), instead of re-reading the file; (b) the file stays the truth and the instance is only a cache, rebuilt by replay after a restart; (c) the dashboard and the session page read the same getters, the browser by live() tail and node from the registry. Not done in this slice; it is in process.md, 'raw deltas in, an instance out'. (2) Temperature: don't chase it. The SDK passes none, and newer models accept only the default of 1.0, so repeated runs already vary. To get varied runs we can compare, vary what is controllable: the angle or framing of the prompt, the model (Haiku, Sonnet or Opus), the effort, and which sources each agent gets. Then count agreement between independent agents (the investigate process's scout and synthesize phases; parallel phases are the next slice). Plan for the rest of this run: finish run 1 of the build process (now on improve-plan); index the agent-context/tools/Item maps from a sub-readme; make the spend gate treat budgets as estimates, with a hard stop only near 10x; then restart Servex last.

To vscode-mastermind, on Follow-up 2 (commit 4bda99041 on task/process-system). (1) The shape is a proposal in ai/doc/code-shape.md; nothing has moved. Classes shared by the browser and node stay in core/ (Item, Task, Session, Process). The front end stays in framework/ai/. The Servex root is the host. Servex/agents/ is the AI part, with subfolders sdk/, tools/, dispatch/, loops/ (TaskLoop, ProcessRunner, Heartbeat, Landed and Lifecycle move in) and spend/; asks/ and cards/ move in too. That is about 70 import lines, as one scripted move once the owner approves. Rejected alternative: a Servex/ai/ folder, because Servex/ai/log.jsonl is already a data folder (the Sessions decision log). (2) Improvements: each folder keeps <folder>/improvements.jsonl, written with item({path:'<folder url>/improvements.jsonl', delta:{tasks:{add:{title,why}}}}). The item tool now reads that file as a Task list and always nests the entries there (probed). The rule is in the mastermind role readme. It is JSONL, not .md, because it is a record. (3) Item vs log is settled in Servex/doc/item-tool.md: item is for files a class reads (it instantiates, checks the delta or method, and returns computed state); the existing Servex log tool is the plainly named raw append, where node stamps the time, author and session and checks the line against its schema. (4) Records are JSONL, prose is markdown. (5) Tailing docs: not by default. Proposed: an agent follows only its own brief and task log, gets a one-line change notice at its next turn boundary through follow/updates, and a rule change goes into the role readme. findings.text: The daily respawn will probably never fire for the real architect. `held()` treats any `state === "stopped"` as "stopped on purpose" (Servex/agents/Respawn.js:101), but the Lifecycle reaper stops idle agents whose task has landed with no `by` (Servex/Lifecycle.js:277, 310). The process-system task already reads `complete` (process.md Status), and `mastermind-system-architect` is not in the reaper's standing-agent list (Lifecycle.js:245). So after a quiet day the architect is reaped, and Respawn then skips it forever. Fix: test `row.stopped_by` alone (a reaped row has none), or add the id to the reaper's exemption list, and add a test for "reaped idle, a day old → respawned".

Requirement 2 says "completion is automatic", but process.md:143 records a known break: a landed task that gets new open children still reads `complete`. This diff now makes that case common, because requests add tasks to other agents' task logs (page_tools.js:225–249). A request added to a landed task stays invisible to completion. Adding an open child to a complete task should reopen it, in Task's replay, with a test.

Most of this diff is outside requirements.md: the session menu and settings, Respawn, requests as logged items, the `design` process, the one-stream design and the docs-vs-logs rule. Each follows a later owner dictation. The brief's own deliverables (Process, ProcessRunner, process.md, run 1, the "document per prompt" rule in mastermind.md:20) landed in earlier commits (b8d7e49f9, 60808be61). Splitting this into separate branches would make each merge easier to judge.

The session menu changes a page (core/Page/Columns.js:48, Page.css:661, AISessionDetail.js:116), but no shot shows it. The only shots in this folder are the 404s from the earlier review (review/report.md finding 1). The button, its popover and `/settings/` need one shot each at 400 and 1200 from a served worktree before the merge.

Respawn's list is a hard-coded static holding one dated folder path (Respawn.js:74–78). A simpler way: a `fresh_daily: true` flag on the spawn spec or registry row, read by the tick. Then the next standing agent needs no code edit, and the path is not copied into a second place.

SessionSettings saves model, effort and notify, but nothing reads them yet (core/Session/doc/menu.md, "Not built yet"). This is stated honestly. Still, an owner who sets "Model: Opus" today gets no effect and no warning on the form. Add one line on the Settings page saying so.

Any caller that is not the log's own agent counts as an asker (page_tools.js:225), including `owner` from the browser and a parent adding steps to its minion's task. Each of those adds now sends the receiver a chat notice. That is probably intended, but messaging.md:164 should say that parent-to-child adds count too.
The `hooks` line in page_tools.js:642 now holds two trailing `//` comments one after the other, and the second one is cut off from its key. Put each comment on its own key.
